graph.title: Reaction game (micro:bit)
notes: This is a software project. The micro:bit's onboard buttons A and B and its 5x5 LED matrix are used, so there is no external wiring, breadboard or LEDs.

The micro:bit was left unconnected in the previous graph. It is now joined to a computer by a USB cable, which is how the MakeCode program (.hex file) gets onto it. The manual doesn't name the cable or computer, so this is an assumption.
The micro:bit is not in the catalogue, so a new 'microbit' part type was added. Its ports are the onboard buttons, LED matrix, USB and battery connector.
The manual doesn't mention a battery, so none is included. The micro:bit is assumed to run on USB power.

Program logic from the manual and block images: forever { pause 1000; pause random(4000); show image; pause 1000; clear screen }, then while (not button A pressed) and (not button B pressed) { pause 20 }, then if A pressed show an arrow pointing to player A, and if B pressed show an arrow pointing to player B.

The first block image shows an empty 'while not A pressed and [empty]'. The second shows the finished nested form 'not A pressed and not B pressed'. The text confirms the final form is not A AND not B.
The optional 'Keep score' challenge uses variables playerA and playerB, set to 0 on start and incremented for the winner. It needs no extra hardware.
